instruction: Access the initial link in the newest Bills folder email and view it in Chrome.

metadata.explanation: Variation 6: Uses 'access' and 'view' verbs. Task requires accessing the first link (https://www.amazon.com/) from the newest Bills email and viewing it in Chrome. Evaluator checks for the presence of all three URLs in open Chrome tabs.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator verifies ALL three URLs (apple.com, scholar.google.com, amazon.com) must be present, but only amazon.com should be verified as the user action
The first two URLs (apple.com, scholar.google.com) are pre-opened in config setup, NOT opened by the user - evaluator cannot distinguish setup state from user action
Instruction requires accessing 'the initial link' (singular) from the email, but evaluator checks for multiple pre-existing tabs
If user closes any pre-opened tab during task execution, evaluation incorrectly fails even though task was completed
The metric 'is_expected_tabs' uses list equality check which is order-sensitive - if amazon.com appears in different tab position, evaluation may fail
Evaluator conflates environment setup with task verification - it verifies setup state rather than user's specific action
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Change expected URLs to only verify amazon.com is present in open tabs: urls: ['https://www.amazon.com/']
Use a different metric that checks if amazon.com was newly added, not just present
Use 'is_expected_active_tab' metric instead to verify the active/focused tab is amazon.com
Add a metric that checks tab count increased by 1 and the new tab is amazon.com
